To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the auditory system uses predictive processing to construct auditory objects.

the auditory system continuously extracts and represents regularities in the auditory scene, and that these regularities are used to predict the future and to parse the incoming sounds into putative sources.

1) the auditory system continuously searches the acoustic signal for regularities and 2) regularities are used for predicting upcoming sounds and for generating hypotheses about the causal relations in the environment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how the brain constructs auditory objects.
the neural mechanisms that enable auditory perception.

the following topics: 1) The auditory system as a predictive processor of information. 2) The neural representation of regularities in sound. 3) Auditory object formation. 4) Auditory scene analysis. 5) Auditory stream segregation. 6) Neural mechanisms for auditory grouping and segmentation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the auditory system is a predictive machine that uses its own predictions to construct the auditory scene.
the brain is a prediction machine.

the auditory system uses predictive coding to construct representations of the acoustic input, which are organized into auditory perceptual objects that can be used to make inferences about the world.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the brain uses a hierarchical Bayesian model to generate hypotheses about the causes of the sensory input, with the aim of maximizing the accuracy of the predictions.
the brain uses predictive representations of regularities to construct auditory perceptual objects.
the auditory system uses regularities to construct a predictive model of the auditory world.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the brain does not simply passively receive information about the environment.
the auditory system is equipped with a set of mechanisms for detecting regularities in the acoustic input and using these regularities to generate predictions of the upcoming sounds.
the auditory system is not just a passive transducer but rather a dynamic, goal-directed, and predictive system.
